source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Setup the system to a standard supported configuration.
2. Boot to OS.
3. Remove the Heat sink or Use a Peltier Device to slowly heat the CPU indicated under Configurations to the TWarning Threshold (Monitor the temperature increase via BMC web interface)
4. Once TWarning Threshold is reached, slowly proceed to add heat until TCritical threshold is reached.   (NOTE:  If you go too fast you may only trip the TCritical Threshold)
5. Continue Heating until system resets

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. System will shutdown once TCritical Threshold has been reached
2. BMC error log will show an over-temperature condition has been detected on CPUx
3. Temperature LED will light if there is one on the Diagnostic Panel
4. If there is a LCD Panel (Aria),  CPU Over Temp error information will be displayed with details of affected CPU
5. Corresponding CPU lightpath will light
6. Front Panel Fault Light will Light
7. Once all checks are complete in during run time, reboot the system and check the uEFI SEL to ensure the corresponding log for CPU Over Temp was logged properly as well as the system reseta

original_test_intent: Drive a named CPU through warning and critical thermal protection and verify shutdown, logs and every physical indicator, but the prescribed heating method lacks an approved safe control envelope.
original_method: An engineer removes the heatsink or applies a Peltier heater while watching BMC WebUI and continues until system reset.
manual_activity: After a safe method is approved, an engineer operates the physical thermal fixture and observes LEDs/LCD; automation may collect telemetry and logs.
required_inputs: Expected shutdown, SEL, LED/LCD/lightpath and recovery matrix
safety_requirements: Do not remove a powered CPU heatsink or heat until reset without vendor approval and interlocks.
Use independent calibrated temperature and emergency cooling.
Safety-stop before hardware damage; no automatic retry.
Preserve first trip evidence and validate cooling before reboot.
agent_execution_scope: Only after method correction, record independent/BMC temperature, host power, SEL and recovery timelines.
Do not apply heat, visually certify indicators or issue verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve/operate fixture, observe physical indicators and recover cooling.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Warm reboot cycling does not test thermal protection and is rejected.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No automated stimulus until a vendor-approved interlocked thermal method is supplied.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: TWarning, TCritical, heat-until-reset source method, all indicators and 10/5 minutes remain as source facts.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a calibrated interlocked thermal fixture with independent sensing, controlled ramp/dwell and hard abort; correlate protection, physical indicators, SEL and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: CPU/platform thermal qualification and protection limits.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces uncontrolled heatsink removal/heat-until-reset with bounded interlocked stimulus.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Retains warning/critical/shutdown and indicator coverage without accepting damaging practice.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Thermal overstress can permanently damage CPU/board.

project_override_considerations: A chamber or firmware injection cannot silently substitute for local CPU heating; any approved alternate must document equivalent sensor/protection coverage.

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The code is reused at row 1527 for unrelated warm reboot cycling, and DeepSeek imports it. The primary source is also unsafe without choosing and bounding a valid heating method.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The only source options include powered heatsink removal or unbounded heating until reset. This is a genuine safety-method blocker, not merely a missing project parameter.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Defines an interlocked unblock condition and preserves manual indicator limits.

review_improvement: Prevents a damaging thermal method while retaining all CPU protection and physical-indicator obligations.
independent_technical_reasoning: A sensor trip can be tested only if stimulus rate and absolute temperature remain controlled; continuing until reset without calibrated limits can overshoot protection and damage hardware.
